methodEvaluationMatrix.name: CTC Frame-Posterior Viterbi Forced Alignment (Log-Domain)
methodEvaluationMatrix.architecture: Wav2Vec2-CTC / Conformer-CTC / MMS-FA + Log-Domain Viterbi Trellis
pros: True acoustic frame-to-character Viterbi alignment with mathematically verifiable monotonicity
No emission-delay bias typical of causal RNN-T transducers
Reuses pure TypeScript log-domain aligner already implemented in SHAHAB workspace
cons: Requires a verified Persian CTC acoustic model checkpoint (.onnx) not yet bundled on disk
Sensitive to unexpanded numeric literals unless spoken-form normalization is provided

methodEvaluationMatrix.name: Active Zipformer-Transducer Emission Frame Mapping
pros: Uses active SHAHAB ASR model family directly without a second runtime
Provides monotonic BPE emission frame indices at 40ms granularity
cons: RNN-T emission frames reflect decoder emission time (lookahead delay), NOT exact phoneme onset/offset
40ms frame stride limits sub-frame precision; ONNX weights currently absent from container snapshot

methodEvaluationMatrix.name: Acoustic Signal VAD Speech-Region Anchoring (Honest Segment-Level)
methodEvaluationMatrix.architecture: Deterministic 20ms RMS + Spectral-Flatness Speech Activity Anchoring
pros: Zero external weight dependency; operates on real PCM signal energy/spectrum
Detects silent/mismatched audio and anchors real speech spans honestly at segment granularity
Refuses to fabricate word-level timestamps when acoustic word evidence is absent
cons: Cannot resolve word-level acoustic boundaries inside continuous speech
Words inside anchored segments remain explicitly TIMING_UNAVAILABLE

methodEvaluationMatrix.name: Phoneme-Level Forced Alignment (Persian G2P + MFA / Kaldi)
methodEvaluationMatrix.architecture: Persian Grapheme-to-Phoneme + Acoustic Triphone/HMM-DNN Forced Aligner
pros: Highest theoretical phoneme/word onset accuracy when backed by a Persian lexicon + G2P
cons: Requires native Kaldi/MFA toolchain + verified Persian pronunciation dictionary (heavy footprint)
Out-of-vocabulary colloquial Persian forms require robust G2P rules

methodEvaluationMatrix.name: Evenly Distributed / Character-Proportional Word Timing
methodEvaluationMatrix.architecture: Heuristic text-length division over segment duration
cons: Fabricates fake acoustic timing — strictly PROHIBITED by SHAHAB-025 §18
Breaks on pauses, elongated vowels, fast/slow speech rate changes, and silent padding

limitations: Active SHAHAB ASR model is an RNN-T transducer (40ms frame stride); emission frames are decoder emission times, not exact acoustic phoneme boundaries.
No standalone Persian CTC/phoneme forced-alignment ONNX checkpoint is bundled in models/persian-ctc-aligner/; SEPARATE_ALIGNER_REQUIRED for production phoneme-exact word timing.
No human-annotated Persian word-boundary ground-truth dataset is bundled in the workspace; real-world Persian word-boundary MAE remains NOT_MEASURED until gold annotations are ingested.

When only PCM audio + transcript are supplied without CTC log-probs or transducer emission frames, SHAHAB-025 anchors real speech segments via acoustic VAD and leaves internal words honestly TIMING_UNAVAILABLE (never fabricating proportional splits).
capabilities.recommendedNextStep: Acquire a permissively licensed Persian/multilingual CTC acoustic model (e.g. Wav2Vec2-CTC / MMS-FA ONNX) and evaluate boundary MAE/P95 against a human-annotated Persian forced-alignment corpus.
